transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM), Lena Morales (Skyline Head of MLOps), Dr. Ethan Park (Skyline CTO), Jonas Weber (Platform Eng), Amira Haddad (Security)

Summary:
Quick renewal/check-in to align on Skyline's request for a retainer uplift, activation of EU region, and initial on‑prem/VPC pilot. Security questions around KMS/HSM and audit logs; cost/latency tradeoffs discussed; agreed to amendment + planning session.

Topics:
- Current usage and headroom
- EU region activation timeline and data residency
- VPC vs on‑prem pilot options + hardware matrix
- SOC2 / KMS / audit logs & egress concerns
- Pricing and billing cadence for retainer uplift

Action items (as captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — retainer uplift, EU region, and VPC/onprem pilot. How are you all doing?
[00:07] Lena Morales: Good, thanks Maya. Busy quarter, lots of inference. We hit about 1.8x of our committed tokens last month so wanna talk buffer.
[00:14] Ethan Park: Sorry for joining late, the timezone thing — quick heads up we got a security review next week so want to make sure the KMS flow is nailed down.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Totally. Omar, wanna jump into current throughput numbers?
[00:25] Omar Patel: Yeah, from our side we looked at your dashboard — average QPS spikes to ~420 during peak, 95th latency about 240ms on Redwood hosted in us-west, prefix cache hit's at about 18% so there's room. If we add EU region you'll see better latency for EU customers but there's cost to replicate KV cache, and also consistent model variants across regions matter.
[00:46] Jonas Weber: Quick clarification: when you say cache replication cost, do you mean cross-region KV sync or separate caches per region?
[00:50] Omar Patel: Right, two options. Separate caches per region keeps latency low but increases memory footprint; cross-region sync reduces memory but adds tail latency on misses. For predictable SLOs we usually recommend per-region caches for user-facing queries.
[01:05] Lena Morales: That makes sense. Our tolerances — 95th under 200ms for EU folks ideally. Is that realistic?
[01:11] Omar Patel: With dedicated capacity in eu-west and quantized model variants, yes—should be achievable. If you go for hosted multi-region we can route EU traffic to EU cluster, fallback to US if capacity constrained. Tradeoff is cost and eventual consistency of sessions.
[01:26] Ethan Park: Are there any notable differences in model outputs when you run the quantized variant? We've seen a small regression on hallucination rate in our internal bench.
[01:33] Omar Patel: Good point. There can be slight quality delta — we can run a quick eval against your prompt set during the pilot and produce a quality delta report. Redwood Optimize will flag significant regressions; recommend canarying the quantized build for a subset of traffic.
[01:48] Ravi Singh: Also to add — we can pin model versions per region so you can test in EU before rolling globally.
[01:54] Lena Morales: Great. Now on VPC and on‑prem: Amira can you speak to the security constraints?
[01:59] Amira Haddad: Sure. Primary asks: we need envelope encryption with our KMS, HSM-backed key rotation, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also egress controls — we can't have any data crossing into non-EU datacenters for EU-labeled requests.
[02:16] Maya Chen: For KMS we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations; for onprem we can integrate with HSM but will need an engineering lead on both sides to coordinate network and cert exchange.
[02:27] Omar Patel: There's also a deployment mode we call Redwood Private that runs in your VPC — that gives private control plane and optional onprem package. From a ops perspective we provide the same API surface but you manage the network and keys.
[02:41] Ethan Park: How heavy is the onprem install? We run a mix of AMD and NVIDIA. What's supported?
[02:46] Omar Patel: We support mainstream NVIDIA amps — A10s, A100s — and there is early support for some AMD parts but sanity testing required. I'll send a hardware matrix. The onprem package uses our orchestration + runtime; typical install for a small pilot is 2-3 days with your infra team, plus network/firewall windows.
[03:05] Jonas Weber: Can we run a hybrid — some traffic to hosted, some to onprem?
[03:09] Maya Chen: Yes, smart routing policies can split by policy — region, latency, or tenant. You can also set fallbacks to hosted if onprem capacity is saturated.
[03:18] Amira Haddad: About logs — do you ship full request logs to our S3? We need redact controls for PII.
[03:24] Ravi Singh: We can configure token-level logging, and we've got automatic redaction tools; audit logs can be forwarded to your S3 or your SIEM via secure transfer. We'll share the logging spec.
[03:34] Lena Morales: Ok next — pricing. We need the math for uplifted retainer vs overage.
[03:38] Maya Chen: Right. Quick summary: two options — 1) increase retainer with reserved Dedicated capacity in eu-west plus burst; 2) keep same retainer and add pay-as-you-go hosted for EU. Option 1 gives better unit cost and predictable latency; option 2 is faster to spin up but higher per-token cost. We'll send a side-by-side worksheet.
[03:56] Jonas Weber: For the retainer uplift, can we amortize provisioning over 12 months and have monthly true-ups?
[04:00] Maya Chen: Yes that's common; we'll reflect that in the amendment.
[04:04] Ethan Park: Any compliance artifacts you can send now? ISO/SOC/KMS architecture docs?
[04:08] Maya Chen: Yep — we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report. Amira, if you have specific questions we can set an SSO/SAML + KMS deep dive.
[04:17] Amira Haddad: Please. Also need encryption in transit diagrams.
[04:20] Omar Patel: One more ops note — during provision we recommend a two-week canary in EU with 10-15% traffic for validation, then full cutover. We'll prepare rollback steps.
[04:30] Lena Morales: Sounds good. Timeline-wise we want EU region live before end of August. Is that feasible?
[04:35] Omar Patel: For dedicated eu-west yes if amendment signed by 7/25 we can hit an 6‑week lead (so end of August). Onprem pilot may require extra time depending on hardware availability.
[04:45] Maya Chen: Great — recap of next steps and owners.
[04:48] Ethan Park: Thanks everyone.
[04:50] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the amendment and scheduling links.

Meeting recap (quick):
- Agreed to prepare retainer amendment with EU dedicated pricing.
- Redwood to provide onprem hardware matrix and install checklist.
- Customer to share KMS/HSM contacts and latency/traffic targets.
- Plan pilot canary in EU followed by full activation.

Links referenced: security pack (link sent via email), draft pricing worksheet (to be shared), onprem checklist (to be attached in follow-up).

End of transcript.
